title: Commission reversal is proportioned against the order GRAND TOTAL (delivery + COD surcharge + GST), not the merchandise value the commission was charged on — a fully returned order never fully reverses the commission and the row is never marked 'cancelled'
detail: prepareCommissionReversal computes `const orderTotal = Number(c.orderTotalPaise ?? 0); const share = orderTotal > 0 ? Math.floor((earned * Math.min(refundPaise, orderTotal)) / orderTotal) : earned;` (commissions.ts:283-285). `orderTotalPaise` is written by placeOrder as `summary.totalPaise` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:948), i.e. `net + deliveryPaise + codSurchargePaise + taxPaise` (checkout.ts:432). The commission itself, however, was charged against `eligiblePaise = subtotalPaise - discountPaise` (checkout.ts:925) and that number is already stored on the commission row (`eligiblePaise`, commissions.ts:216). The refund that reaches the reversal is merchandise-only: requestReturnOrReplacement writes `refundAmountPaise = lineTotal - discountShare` and its own comment says "Delivery/tax are order-level and not refunded on a partial item return" (functions/src/returns/requests.ts:96-102), and adminApproveOrderRequest passes exactly that amount through (functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:91,105). So the numerator is merchandise value while the denominator includes delivery/COD/GST, and the reversal is systematically short on EVERY return. Because `reversedTotal < earned`, the `status: 'cancelled'` branch at commissions.ts:304 is also never taken, so the row stays 'confirmed' and the residual stays withdrawable (it is still picked up by the settlement query in withdrawals.ts:130-139, whose `net = commissionPaise - reversedPaise` is > 0).
failure_scenario: Seeded settings (scripts/seed.ts:178-180: standardFeePaise ₹49, codSurchargePaise ₹20, freeDeliveryOverPaise ₹1499). Customer B uses affiliate A's code on a COD order: 1 item, subtotal ₹1000, no coupon. eligiblePaise = 100000, A's rate 5% → commissionPaise = 5000; orderTotalPaise = 100000 + 4900 + 2000 = 106900. Order is delivered → commission 'confirmed', A's confirmedBalancePaise +5000. B returns the only item; refundAmountPaise = 100000. Admin approves the return: share = floor(5000 × 100000 / 106900) = 4677, claw = 4677. A keeps 323 paise of WITHDRAWABLE balance on an order that was refunded in full, and the commission row is left status 'confirmed', reversedPaise 4677, never 'cancelled'. The gap scales with the non-merchandise share: with GST charged on top (gstEnabled && !pricesIncludeTax, gstRate 0.18) it is ~15% of every commission; with a flat per-unit commissionPaise it is the same fraction of a much larger number (a ₹100/unit commission on a ₹200 COD item leaves ₹22.90 unreversed).
fix: Proportion against the base the commission was actually charged on: `const base = Number(c.eligiblePaise ?? c.orderTotalPaise ?? 0)` and `share = base > 0 ? Math.floor((earned * Math.min(refundPaise, base)) / base) : earned`. Legacy rows without eligiblePaise keep the old denominator. This makes a full-value return reverse the full commission and correctly trip the `reversedTotal >= earned → status:'cancelled'` branch.

title: confirmCommissionsForOrder credits the full commissionPaise and ignores reversedPaise — a commission reversed while still 'pending' is confirmed in full, driving pendingBalancePaise negative and crediting withdrawable balance that was already clawed back
detail: confirmCommissionsForOrder selects rows with `status === 'pending'` and moves `const amount = Number(c.commissionPaise ?? 0)` from pendingBalancePaise to confirmedBalancePaise + lifetimeEarningsPaise (commissions.ts:341-352). It never subtracts `reversedPaise`. prepareCommissionReversal explicitly supports reversing a row that is still 'pending' — `const balanceKey = wasConfirmed ? 'confirmedBalancePaise' : 'pendingBalancePaise'` (commissions.ts:289-290) — and on a partial claw it leaves the row's status untouched (commissions.ts:304, the 'cancelled' stamp only lands when reversedTotal >= earned). The two therefore double-count. The window is real and documented in the code: settleDeliveryCommissions runs AFTER and OUTSIDE the status transaction, and its own doc-comment says "it can abort on contention while the order is already 'delivered' ... a failure here is recoverable by simply marking the order delivered again" (functions/src/orders/status.ts:31-51). While the order is 'delivered' with the commission still 'pending', a return is fully legal — requestReturnOrReplacement only checks `o.status !== 'delivered'` (functions/src/returns/requests.ts:44). Note finding #1 makes EVERY reversal a partial one, so the row essentially always stays 'pending' rather than becoming 'cancelled'. The same 'ignores reversedPaise' pattern exists in the cancel path (functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:171, `FieldValue.increment(-amount)` with the gross), but cancellation is unreachable after delivery (TRANSITIONS in status.ts:15-23 and CANCELLABLE in checkout.ts:1143 both stop before 'delivered'), so only the confirm path is exploitable.
failure_scenario: Order with commissionPaise 5000 is marked delivered; the status transaction commits but confirmCommissionsForOrder throws (contention/transient) — order.status = 'delivered', order.affiliateCommissionStatus still 'pending', commission row still 'pending', affiliate pendingBalancePaise 5000. Customer requests a return the same day; admin approves it, clawing 2000: pendingBalancePaise 5000 → 3000, row reversedPaise 2000, status still 'pending'. Admin re-marks the order delivered (the documented delivered→delivered re-entry, status.ts:92-99) → confirmCommissionsForOrder credits the FULL 5000: pendingBalancePaise 3000 − 5000 = −2000, confirmedBalancePaise +5000, lifetimeEarningsPaise +5000. The affiliate can now request and be paid ₹50 on a commission of which ₹20 had already been reversed, and their pending balance is permanently negative.
fix: In confirmCommissionsForOrder use `const amount = Math.max(0, Number(c.commissionPaise ?? 0) - Number(c.reversedPaise ?? 0))` and skip the row (still stamping it 'confirmed'/'cancelled') when that is <= 0. Apply the same net-of-reversal amount in orders/cancel.ts:171 for symmetry.

title: Commissions already marked 'paid' by a withdrawal are silently excluded from reversal — a return after payout claws back nothing and records no shortfall, defeating the unrecoveredPaise mechanism
detail: prepareCommissionReversal keeps only rows whose status is 'confirmed' or 'pending' (commissions.ts:265-269); a row whose status is 'paid' is dropped before any accounting happens, so neither `reversedPaise` nor `unrecoveredPaise` is written and no balance is touched. approveWithdrawal is what stamps rows 'paid' (functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:194-206). This directly contradicts the stated intent of the adjacent code: "The affiliate may already have withdrawn this money. Never drive a balance negative — bank what we can and record the shortfall so it is visible rather than silently absorbed" (commissions.ts:294-296). Because a withdrawn commission is exactly the case that turns a row 'paid', that shortfall path can never fire for the case it was written for; the shortfall IS silently absorbed and the affiliate's remaining confirmed balance (earned on other orders) is never used to recover it. This is compounded by the settlement loop itself: it marks a row fully 'paid' even when `remaining` only partly covers it (withdrawals.ts:192-206 — `remaining -= net` is allowed to go negative and the loop only breaks on the NEXT iteration), so a row can become permanently un-reversible after only part of it was actually paid out.
failure_scenario: Affiliate A has two confirmed commissions: ₹60 on order X and ₹40 on order Y, plus ₹500 of confirmed balance from older orders. A requests ₹550; the admin approves. approveWithdrawal deducts ₹550 from confirmedBalancePaise and walks the oldest-first settlement query marking rows 'paid' until `remaining <= 0` — X's row is marked 'paid'. Three days later customer B returns order X in full and the admin approves the return. prepareCommissionReversal loads X's commission, sees status 'paid', and drops it: no reversal, reversedPaise stays 0, unrecoveredPaise stays 0, A's remaining confirmed balance is untouched even though the merchant refunded the customer in full. The commission ledger and every admin/affiliate screen continue to report ₹60 legitimately earned on a fully refunded order, with no record that anything is owed back.
fix: Include 'paid' rows in the reversal filter and let the existing recovered/unrecovered split do its job: recover what the affiliate's current confirmedBalancePaise can cover (never below 0) and record the remainder in unrecoveredPaise so it is visible to the admin. Separately, stop the settlement loop from marking a row 'paid' when `remaining < net` (settle only up to `remaining`, or leave the row unsettled).

title: A per-variant commissionPaise explicitly set to 0 is ignored and the affiliate's percentage rate is paid instead — and with isAffiliateEligible hardcoded true there is no other way to zero a product's commission
detail: lineAccrual only honours the flat per-unit figure when `Number.isFinite(perUnit) && perUnit > 0` (commissions.ts:112-115); a stored 0 falls through to the product rate and then to the affiliate's flat `affiliate.commissionRate` (commissions.ts:116-122). checkout.ts:115 deliberately propagates an explicit 0 (`if (v.commissionPaise != null) commissionPaise = Number(v.commissionPaise)`) and priceLines only nulls a non-finite value (checkout.ts:132), so 0 reaches accrual as a real, admin-chosen value. The admin form distinguishes the two: `commissionPaise: r.comm === '' ? null : toPaise(r.comm)` (admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:262,279) — blank means "unset", typing 0 means "zero". The only other opt-out, `isAffiliateEligible`, is written `true` at product creation and at bulk import (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:199,387) and is not editable anywhere in the admin, and `affiliateCommissionRate` is likewise always written null (same lines). So an admin has no working way to say 'this product/variant pays no affiliate commission'.
failure_scenario: Admin edits a ₹2,000 product and sets the commission field on the 'Large' variant to 0, intending that variant to earn nothing (it is sold near cost). Variant doc gets commissionPaise: 0. A referred customer buys one Large: checkout embeds commissionPaise 0 on the order item, lineAccrual sees perUnit = 0, falls through to the affiliate's 5% rate and accrues 10000 paise (₹100) instead of 0 — money the merchant explicitly configured away. The product page and the admin form both say 0.
fix: Treat a non-null per-unit figure as authoritative regardless of value: keep `commissionPaise: number | null` on CommissionLine and branch on `l.commissionPaise != null && Number.isFinite(l.commissionPaise) && l.commissionPaise >= 0` returning `Math.max(0, Math.floor(perUnit * l.qty))` (0 included). Optionally also expose isAffiliateEligible in the product form.

title: Web affiliate history renders every commission as a positive credit regardless of status or reversal, while the app renders the status — the two clients disagree about the same shared `commissions` documents
detail: The web activity feed pushes one row per commission with `amount: formatMoneySigned(c.commissionPaise, 'credit', 2)` and `subtitle: \`${commissionRatePercent(c.commissionRate)}% commission · …\`` (page.tsx:111-120). It never reads `c.status` and never subtracts `c.reversedPaise`, so a commission that was cancelled by an order cancellation (functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:172-176) or reversed by an approved return (commissions.ts:301-306) is still shown to the affiliate as money earned, in green, with no qualifier — while the balance cards above it have already dropped. The app renders the same documents correctly: affiliate_wallet_screen.dart:229-256 maps status to 'Confirmed' / 'Paid out' / 'Cancelled' / 'Pending · clears on delivery' and greys cancelled rows, and the app dashboard excludes cancelled rows from its month total (affiliate_dashboard_screen.dart:171-179). Balances themselves are correct on both clients; this is a reporting drift on a shared collection.
failure_scenario: Affiliate A earns ₹50 on order #BRK-48123. The customer cancels the order; performCancellation sets the commission row to status 'cancelled' and removes ₹50 from A's pendingBalancePaise. On the app A sees the row as 'Cancelled', greyed. On the web A sees 'Priya referred · #BRK-48123 — 5% commission' with '+₹50.00' in green, and a pending balance that does not include it — A reports a missing ₹50 to support.
fix: Mirror the app: read `c.status` (and `c.reversedPaise`) in withdrawalOutcome's commission counterpart — show 'Cancelled'/'Paid out'/'Confirmed'/'Pending' in the subtitle and render cancelled rows neutral rather than as a green credit.

title: The app's withdrawal screen never shows the processing fee or the net payout the affiliate will actually receive, while the web does
detail: AffiliateRepository exposes `feePaise()` and `netPayoutPaise()` that mirror requestWithdrawal's arithmetic exactly (app/lib/features/affiliate/data/affiliate_repository.dart:24-34), and the screen loads AffiliateSettings in initState (affiliate_withdraw_screen.dart:43-45), but only `minWithdrawalPaise` is ever used (affiliate_withdraw_screen.dart:210,419) — neither fee method is referenced anywhere in app/lib. The web withdraw page shows a 'Processing fee' / 'You receive' summary computed with the same formula before the affiliate confirms (web/src/app/(shop)/account/affiliate/withdraw/page.tsx:41-42,189-198). The server still records the correct net (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:56-58) and both clients render `paidAmountPaise` afterwards, so no money is mis-moved; the app user simply confirms a gross figure and is later shown a smaller credited amount with no prior disclosure. Harmless with the seeded fee of 0 (scripts/seed.ts:207-209), wrong the moment a fee is configured.
failure_scenario: Admin sets settings/affiliate.processingFeeType 'fixed', processingFeeValue 2000 (₹20). An affiliate on the app taps 'Withdraw all' for ₹500 and confirms; the screen showed ₹500 throughout. approveWithdrawal records paidAmountPaise 48000 and the wallet feed then reads '−₹480 · Amount credited to your bank account.' — a ₹20 discrepancy the app never disclosed, while a web user doing the same saw 'Processing fee ₹20 / You receive ₹480' before confirming.
fix: Render `_settings.feePaise(_amountPaise)` and `_settings.netPayoutPaise(_amountPaise)` in the withdraw card (the helpers already exist and match the server), matching the web summary block.

title: App bank-account edit keeps `verifiedAt` when the account number or IFSC changes; web nulls it — doc-shape drift on the shared customers/{uid}.bankAccounts array
detail: Web's BankForm rebuilds the record with `verifiedAt: existing && existing.ifsc === ifscU && existing.accountNumberMasked === maskAccountNumber(acct) ? existing.verifiedAt : null` — any change to the number or the IFSC invalidates a prior verification (web/src/components/account/BankForm.tsx:87-90). The app's updateBankAccount spreads `...current` and overwrites only accountHolderName / accountNumberMasked / ifsc / bankName / branch / updatedAt (affiliate_repository.dart:302-311), so `verifiedAt` survives a changed account number or IFSC. Every other field of the record is byte-identical between the two clients (id, accountHolderName, `•••• last4` mask — same U+2022 sequence, ifsc upper-cased, bankName, branch-or-null, isDefault, createdAt, updatedAt), so this is the only drift found on the shared array. Nothing in the codebase currently reads verifiedAt (no reference in functions/, admin/ or either client outside the write paths), which is why this is low rather than higher.
failure_scenario: An affiliate adds an account on the web that an admin later stamps verifiedAt. On the app they edit the same entry and enter a different account number: the array now holds a record whose accountNumberMasked is '•••• 9911' while verifiedAt still points at the verification of '•••• 4321'. Any future feature (or manual admin check) that trusts verifiedAt to mean 'these details were verified' pays out to an unverified account.
fix: In updateBankAccount, set `'verifiedAt': null` whenever `hasNewNumber` is true or the normalised IFSC differs from `current['ifsc']`, matching BankForm.tsx:87-90.
